title: Usage Chronicle reconciliation and rollback runner
creator: Priya Shah
description:
Build a resilient, auditable scheduled reconciliation and rollback runner ("Usage Chronicle") that compares high-throughput streaming consumption aggregates with the canonical billing ledger and issues safe, idempotent adjustments when discrepancies are detected. Goal: reduce manual late-arrival corrections to under 2% of monthly credits and provide transparent dry-run and audit controls surfaced in Console.

Background:
- Current streaming aggregator emits per-route/per-tenant deltas into compacted topics and a nearline aggregator writes provisional consumption snapshots. Late events and cross-region failovers occasionally cause divergence between provisional aggregates and the billing ledger, triggering manual investigations and customer credits.
- We need a single service that can run deterministic reconciliation sweeps, compute minimal rollback or credit actions, and execute them with strict auditing and safety gates (dry-run, canary, SLA-aware throttling).

Scope / What this ticket delivers:
1) A scheduled reconciliation runner that:
   - Streams from the compacted consumption topic and joins with the billing ledger snapshot to compute per-tenant delta vectors for a configurable window.
   - Uses a watermarking policy and allowed-lateness parameter to include late-arriving records.
   - Produces a reconciliation diff stream with scoring for confidence and required action (noop, offset-adjust, credit-issue, manual-review).
2) Safe execution framework:
   - Dry-run mode that writes proposed actions to an audit bucket and Console review queue.
   - Canary execution for a small tenant subset with rollback capability.
   - Idempotent action executor that applies credits/offsets via the canonical billing API with deduplication tokens and signed operation metadata.
3) Observability and Console support:
   - Reconciliation run metrics (processed messages, late-event rate, delta-sum by tenant tier, action counts).
   - Per-run audit artifacts (signed manifests, sample traces) surfaced in Console under Billing -> Reconciliations.
4) Migration and Safeguards:
   - Bulk-readback path to undo a reconciliation run (rollback manifest) in case of operator error.
   - Quota/throughput throttles to avoid overwhelming billing backend during large runs.

Design decisions and trade-offs considered:
- Exactly-once vs at-least-once: achieving strict exactly-once across streaming join + billing mutations is costly. We opt for at-least-once ingestion with idempotent execution (dedupe tokens + operation signatures) so actions can be retried safely.
- Reconciliation frequency: daily vs hourly. Start with nightly full-window sweeps plus hourly incremental probes for high-traffic tenants. This balances cost and detection latency.
- Compute model: Beam/Flink running on our k8s cluster vs lightweight consumer+batcher service. We will implement core join logic in a Beam job for stable watermarking and late-arrival handling, and keep the executor as a separate stateless service that reads the diff stream.

Acceptance criteria:
- Nightly reconciliation job completes within the configured SLA (6 hours for full production run) on staging with production-sized snapshot.
- Dry-run outputs are persisted and accessible in Console for at least 30 days.
- Idempotent executor successfully applies credits for a canary tenant subset (end-to-end test with a synthetic divergence).
- Rollback manifest can revert an executed run within 30 minutes without manual database repair.
- Alerts trigger when run anomaly rate (manual-review decisions) exceeds 0.5% of processed tenants.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Design doc and data contracts (compact topic schema, reconciliation-diff schema, audit manifest format) — owner: Priya — due 2026-02-27.
2) Beam job: join streaming aggregates with ledger snapshot; emit reconciliation-diff topic — owner: Data Infra team (Miguel) — PoC by 2026-03-05.
3) Executor service: idempotent apply/undo APIs, dry-run writer, canary selection — owner: Billing Backend (Miguel) — initial implementation by 2026-03-12.
4) Console integration: UI for run history, dry-run review queue, signed-manifest download — owner: Console PM/Design — integration by 2026-03-18.
5) End-to-end canary and load test on staging, iterate — target 2026-03-22.

Runbook and operator controls:
- Manual stop: reconciliation job subscribes to a coordinator flag (feature-flagged run id). Toggling the flag stops new executors from applying actions.
- Emergency rollback: use rollback manifest to produce compensating operations; executor supports reverse-mode.
- Safety limits: per-tenant max-credit cap and global daily credit throttle.

Metrics and dashboards:
- Reconciliation: run_duration_seconds, processed_tenants, late_event_rate_pct, action_count_by_type, manual_review_rate, rollback_success_rate.
- Business: estimated_credit_impact_usd, customers_affected_count, median_time_to_detect_divergence.

Testing strategy:
- Unit tests for diff computation and dedupe token generation.
- Integration tests: staged ledger snapshot vs synthetic compacted topic with injected late events.
- Chaos tests: broker failover, duplicate events, executor restarts.
- End-to-end canary in staging with synthetic tenant that simulates a 5% divergence.

risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Billing backend could be overwhelmed by a large applied run -> Mitigation: global throttle + canary + rate-limited worker pool
Risk: Duplicate events cause double-crediting -> Mitigation: use dedupe tokens and signed operation metadata; executor rejects duplicates
Risk: Incorrect diff algorithm causes false positives -> Mitigation: dry-run mode for 7 days + operator review queue before full-enable
Risk: Sensitive audit data exposure -> Mitigation: manifest encryption at rest (KMS) and limited Console ACLs
